description: A cold-water schooling whitefish that forms an important commercial fishery in the North Pacific.
short description: Cold-water whitefish with mild flavour, widely caught in the North Pacific.
context: WWF notes Alaska pollock shares waters with protected species such as Steller sea lions, Chinook salmon and sharks. Bycatch is relatively low, but bottom trawling can affect sponge beds and sedimentary habitat. These ecosystem and habitat concerns support a Reduce rating.

description: A highly migratory tuna with firm, pale meat, commonly found in temperate and tropical open-ocean waters.
short description: Firm, pale-fleshed tuna found across temperate and tropical open oceans.
context: WWF notes Albacore Tuna is highly migratory and Near Threatened. The cited southern-stock assessment no longer considered the stock overfished or undergoing overfishing, while South African pole-and-line fishing is comparatively selective. These factors support the Best Choice rating for this record.

description: A large, fast-swimming tuna that migrates across the open Atlantic and is highly valued in premium seafood markets.
short description: Large migratory tuna prized for its rich meat and premium seafood appeal.
context: WWF highlights very high bycatch in Atlantic pelagic longlines, including protected seabirds, sharks, marine mammals, turtles and billfishes. Bluefin also occupies a high trophic level, so heavy fishing can affect wider food webs. These impacts support an Avoid rating.

description: A cold-water cod species associated with northern Atlantic waters and valued for its mild, flaky flesh.
short description: Mild, flaky cold-water fish associated with northern Atlantic waters.
context: WWF reports the North-East Arctic cod stock was healthy in its cited assessment and covered by a good management plan. Closures protect juveniles and management measures help control fishing and illegal, unreported and unregulated activity. Despite these positives, this Russian Barents Sea record is rated Reduce.

description: A widely farmed salmon with pink-orange flesh, raised in marine cages and commonly sold fresh or smoked.
short description: Pink-orange salmon widely farmed and sold fresh or smoked.
context: WWF explains that Norwegian floating net-pen salmon farms interact directly with marine waters. Waste, uneaten feed and antibiotics can affect sediments, while escapes, disease, parasites and chemical use can affect ecosystems. These environmental risks support a Reduce rating for this farmed record.

context: WWF notes Chinese Silver Pomfret is mainly caught by trawl. The guide describes trawling as highly detrimental because it is non-selective, can damage habitat and can create bycatch of endangered, threatened and protected species. These fishing-method impacts support an Avoid rating.

short description: Large Pacific salmon known for rich flavour and dark flesh.
context: WWF says cited Alaskan Chinook salmon fisheries are managed by the Alaska Department of Fish and Game and the stocks are healthy. Area-specific commercial regulations, Fishery Improvement Projects and partial MSC certification support management. These measures support the Best Choice classification for this fishery.

short description: Long-bodied cold-water fish from New Zealand with white flesh.
context: WWF notes New Zealand hoki is caught with mid-water otter trawls. Bycatch and juvenile catch can be significant, and interactions with protected species may be high. Discards are low and seabed contact is unlikely, reducing habitat impact. The balance of risks and mitigations leads WWF to Reduce.

Stock health and species biology information is lacking, creating sustainability uncertainty. Purse seine is the common and more selective harvest method, supporting Reduce rather than Avoid.

Regional fisheries are considered significantly overfished, while bottom trawling can threaten turtles and damage corals and other benthic habitats. It is commonly caught by bottom trawl, which is highly detrimental because the gear is non-selective, can damage habitat and can create bycatch of protected species. These risks support Avoid.

Overfishing, habitat destruction, cyanide fishing and fish bombing are major threats, making the Malaysian Sabah wild-caught record an Avoid choice.

Because assessed fisheries use trawls and gillnets and cover vulnerable ray groups, WWF places this record in Avoid to reduce pressure on ray populations and marine ecosystems.

Some farms also depend on trash fish, creating high Fish Feed Dependency Ratios. Although ponds can reduce disease risk versus open cages, WWF still rates this record Avoid and points to AIP alternatives.
